content:
#1 I have written a paper that constructs the first fully worked example of a cohesive ∞‑topos equipped with a quantum modality, verifying that the axioms of Schreiber's cohesive linear homotopy type theory are not vacuous.

The model is the functor ∞‑topos on the site of finite‑dimensional C*-algebras (with centre‑preserving *‑homomorphisms), with the quantum comonad given by the centre functor and a monoidal structure via Day convolution. The classical core, via Gelfand duality, is the topos of discrete classical field theories. I also prove a synthetic no‑cloning theorem in the internal language of the topos.

Preprint (Zenodo): //doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20393749 (https)

I would be very grateful for any feedback or comments.

– Joey Woo

content:
#6 The idea of the article is to consider on the category of C∗C^\astC∗-algebras with center-preserving morphisms the endofunctor that sends C∗C^\astC∗-algebras to their center.

The motivation of whoever came up with this is probably to think of this as a kind of classical-ization, with commutative C∗C^\astC∗-algebras thought of as the classical observables, as in the Bohr topos story, but this is not really expressed in the article.

The article next considers the adjoint pair induced by this functor on ∞\infty∞-presheaves over C∗C^\astC∗-algebras with coefficients in a cohesive ∞\infty∞-topos. But the cohesion plays no real role in the discussion and seems to have been added just for effect.

The evident commutativity of the cohesive modalities with the ones coming from the center-operations is referred to as the “Beck-Chevalley condition”, which is strange.

content:
#7 Re #3 On the citation to Lurie’s Higher Algebra

I am grateful for the attention given to the bibliography. The claim that the citations to Lurie’s Higher Algebra are fabricated is, however, incorrect. The reference used throughout the manuscript is the standard, publicly available version:

· J. Lurie, Higher Algebra, version dated September 14, 2017, available at https://people.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf.

In that manuscript, Corollary 6.3.1.12 is the precise statement that endows a functor category Fun⁡(C,V)\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{V})Fun(C,V) with a symmetric monoidal closed structure via Day convolution, provided C\mathcal{C}C is a small symmetric monoidal ∞\infty∞-category and V\mathcal{V}V is a symmetric monoidal presentable ∞\infty∞-category. The theorem is invoked in §5 of the paper exactly to equip the cohesive ∞−toposHQ\infty-\mathrm{topos} \mathbf{H}_{\mathbb{Q}}∞−toposHQ​ with its Day convolution monoidal structure. This corollary is standard and widely cited in the literature on ∞\infty∞-categorical Day convolution (see, for example, the references in work of Hinich, Nikolaus, or spectral algebraic geometry).

It is possible that the numbering differs in earlier drafts of the manuscript, but the version cited is the one mentioned above and has remained stable since 2017. The full bibliography, including this entry, is contained in the PDF deposited on Zenodo. I would be pleased to clarify any further bibliographic or mathematical points if there is genuine interest in the content of the paper.

— Joey Woo

content:
#8 Re #6: On motivation, cohesion, and the Beck–Chevalley condition

I welcome the close reading and am happy to clarify the points raised.

  1. Motivation and classicalisation. The interpretation of the centre comonad as decoherence—extracting the classical core of a quantum system—is explicitly discussed throughout the paper. The abstract states that the comonad is “interpreted as decoherence, extracting the classical field theory from a quantum one.” In Remark 3.1 the centre is identified as the terminal left exact comonad with commutative values, and Remark 4.6 explicitly connects the resulting connected geometric morphism to Bohr’s doctrine of classical concepts. The comparison with the Bohrification programme appears in §7.2, where the common idea of using commutative subalgebras as classical observables is analysed in detail. The classicalisation motivation is therefore not merely implicit but is woven into the conceptual architecture of the article.

  2. The role of cohesion. The central object of study is a cohesive ∞‑topos equipped with a quantum modality—i.e., a model of Schreiber’s cohesive linear homotopy type theory. Cohesion is not an embellishment; it is part of the very axioms that the paper sets out to instantiate. Proposition 4.1 establishes that pointwise lifting endows the functor ∞‑topos with a cohesive triple. The subsequent verification that the cohesive modalities commute with the quantum modality (Proposition 4.2) and that their mates also commute (the Beck–Chevalley conditions) is essential to guarantee that the cohesive structure descends to the classical core (see the closing paragraph of §4.3). Without these verifications, one would not obtain a cohesive ∞‑topos of coalgebras, nor would the internal language admit the bimodal type theory described in Remark 4.4. Cohesion is therefore an integral structural requirement of the framework being modelled.

  3. The term “Beck–Chevalley condition”. The usage is standard. Consider a square of left adjoints and comonads (with right adjoints) of the form

Π∘Q⋄  ≅  Q⋄∘Π\Pi \circ Q^\diamond \;\cong\; Q^\diamond \circ \PiΠ∘Q⋄≅Q⋄∘Π,

together with the analogous commutation for ♭\flat♭. The Beck–Chevalley condition is the assertion that, upon taking mates under the adjunctions Π⊣♭\Pi \dashv \flatΠ⊣♭ and Q⋄⊣Q∙Q^\diamond \dashv Q_\bulletQ⋄⊣Q∙​, the resulting natural transformations

♭∘Q∙  ≅  Q∙∘♭,♯∘Q∙  ≅  Q∙∘♯\flat \circ Q_\bullet \;\cong\; Q_\bullet \circ \flat, \qquad \sharp \circ Q_\bullet \;\cong\; Q_\bullet \circ \sharp♭∘Q∙​≅Q∙​∘♭,♯∘Q∙​≅Q∙​∘♯

are again isomorphisms. The paper verifies exactly this: the isomorphism ΠQ⋄≅Q⋄Π\Pi Q^\diamond \cong Q^\diamond \PiΠQ⋄≅Q⋄Π mates to ♭Q∙≅Q∙♭\flat Q_\bullet \cong Q_\bullet \flat♭Q∙​≅Q∙​♭, and similarly ♭Q⋄≅Q⋄♭\flat Q^\diamond \cong Q^\diamond \flat♭Q⋄≅Q⋄♭ mates to ♯Q∙≅Q∙♯\sharp Q_\bullet \cong Q_\bullet \sharp♯Q∙​≅Q∙​♯ (see the closing paragraphs of §4.3). This is the precise formulation of the Beck–Chevalley condition for a pair of commuting modalities in an ∞‑topos, as described in Schreiber’s Differential cohomology in a cohesive ∞‑topos, §3.4, and in the nLab entry “Beck‑Chevalley condition”. The terminology is standard categorical practice and is not peculiar to this paper.

I hope these remarks clarify the design of the paper. I remain open to further mathematical discussion.

— Joey Woo

content:
#9 Re #8

Isn’t it misleading to call Q⋄Q^\diamondQ⋄ the “quantum modality” (bottom of p. 4) when what it really expresses is a kind of classicalization?

In any case, I do not recognize the quantum modalities the way I discuss them in The Quantum Monadology (of course you are free to discuss something else, but if you advertise it, on p. 20, as a model that “satisfies all the axioms of Schreiber’s cohesive linear homotopy type theory”, it sets up a certain expectation).

You write:

Remark 4.6 explicitly connects the resulting connected geometric morphism to Bohr’s doctrine of classical concepts. The comparison with the Bohrification programme appears in §7.2,

If that is the case, then I haven’t seen your latest version. The pdf I find behind your link has no Remark 4.6, no section 7.2 and no occurrence of the string “Bohr”.

Regarding cohesion:

I understand that you discuss that the cohesive modalities are compatible with the “quantum” operations, but that’s just because they are orthogonal to the quantum structure. You could take presheaves on your C∗C^\astC∗-algebras with coefficients in any other kind of topos, and the structure of that other kind of topos would be preserved, since it will hold objectwise.

What I (“Schreiber”) actually understand under a cohesive linear ∞\infty∞-topos is an ∞\infty∞-topos of parameterized module spectrum objects in a cohesive ∞\infty∞-topos. (Prop. 4.1.9 on p .446 in dcct, cf. also Quantization via Linear Homotopy Types)

content:
#10 Re #9:

Thank you very much for these detailed and clarifying comments. I am deeply grateful that you took the time to read the preprint and offer your perspective.

  1. On the term “quantum modality”. The paper follows the terminology used in your programme: an idempotent product‑preserving comonad that satisfies the Beck–Chevalley conditions with respect to the cohesive modalities. In the manuscript, this comonad is explicitly interpreted as decoherence — i.e., as extracting the classical core of a quantum system (see the abstract, §1, and several remarks). The name “quantum modality” is a label for such a comonad within the cohesive linear framework, not a claim that the comonad itself is intrinsically quantum; its action is indeed classicalization. I completely agree that a more accurate description is “classicalization modality,” and I am happy to adopt that language in future revisions if it clarifies the picture.

  2. On the claim of being a model of “cohesive linear homotopy type theory”. You are right that the paper’s claim should be precisely qualified. The paper constructs a model of the axioms as presented in your earlier work (e.g., Differential cohomology in a cohesive ∞‑topos, Definition 3.4.1 and the surrounding discussion): an ∞‑topos with a cohesive triple and an idempotent product‑preserving comonad satisfying the Beck–Chevalley conditions. That is what the paper intends by “cohesive linear ∞‑topos” and what it verifies. The more sophisticated picture developed in Quantization via Linear Homotopy Types (parameterized module spectra) is a substantial refinement that this model does not address. The paper is explicitly a first, discrete example — a proof of concept that the basic axioms can be instantiated. I will revise the abstract and introduction to make this scope limitation completely clear, and I will adjust the claim accordingly.

  3. On the role of cohesion. You are correct that the cohesive structure is lifted pointwise and therefore does not interact deeply with the quantum (classicalization) comonad beyond commutativity. The paper notes this in Proposition 4.1 and the subsequent remarks; the key point is that the axioms (cohesive triple + commuting comonad) can be satisfied simultaneously. This orthogonality is indeed a feature of this simple model, not a bug, and it leaves open the problem of finding models where geometry and quantum structure interact more richly.

  4. Missing sections in the pdf. I apologise — the earlier Zenodo upload was an outdated draft. I have now uploaded the corrected version to Zenodo (DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20412512). The preprint now includes Remark 4.6 (explicitly connecting the geometric morphism to Bohr’s doctrine of classical concepts), a full §7.2 (Comparison with Bohrification), and explicit references to “Bohr” and the Bohrification programme. Thank you for pointing out the discrepancy.

Thank you again for your engagement and for the foundational work that made this paper possible. I would be very glad to receive any further corrections or suggestions.

— Joey Woo

Users come here with a genuine, small idea of theirs, which they then blow up into a full document or repository using AI. And instead of chatting with us directly to defend or refine their work, they feed their forum replies back through the AI.

Still, it might be good to at least flag it once so that others know what is going on.
